settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Appearance, language, and what this build is.
settings.appearanceHint: Following the system keeps changing with it while the application is open.

terminal.title: Terminal colours
terminal.hint: A dark terminal in a light interface is a common choice, so the two are decided separately. Either way the sixteen ANSI colours come from the same palette, tuned to be readable on its own background.

session.title: Opening a session
session.hint: The split opens the files for the same host under the terminal, in one tab, and follows the shell's directory — a cd in the terminal takes the panel with it. Either way it can be closed or opened per tab, on the strip under the terminal.

files.title: File browser
files.hint: The tree opens the branches leading to where you are, so the two panes never disagree about where that is.

monitor.title: Host monitor
monitor.hint: The monitor sits to the right of the workspace and reports the host of the terminal on screen: load, memory, network and file systems. It samples about every two seconds, by running a group of read-only commands over the connection that is already open — and it samples nothing at all while it is hidden.
